visibleEvidence: An ivory cover pairs large black serif text and small red identifiers with a frontal green-sofa image.
spatialReading: The sofa dominates a concrete-looking room with an orange perforated screen, roof opening, side glazing, dense greenery and a woven-looking rug. Overhead daylight models the cushions and grounds the base.
brandMeaning: Soft upholstery contrasts with substantial architecture, proposing calm without an empty setting.
application: Borrow daylight, framed greenery and clear product hierarchy; adapt architectural hardness and colours around the exact sofa.
authorityAndLimits: The cover explicitly identifies a draft blueprint; product and material authenticity are unverified.

visibleEvidence: A white serif-led page contains an identity-system inset and a dark motion-sofa banner. The inset shows a red symbol/uppercase wordmark, sans-serif messaging and rounded layered panels.
spatialReading: The banner places an olive seat against wine-coloured surroundings. A person in a dark top and pale trousers reclines with legs supported; tables and a tall vase occupy the right.
brandMeaning: The stated shift is from identity components toward a fuller visual world.
application: Retain supported use and product prominence; distinguish graphic panels from room treatments.
authorityAndLimits: The page asserts an evolution; it does not independently establish adoption or chronology.

visibleEvidence: Four image groups accompany a five-language diagnosis: small promotional cards, a wine/olive sofa banner, a daylight mattress room and a dark neck-device portrait.
spatialReading: The mattress sits centrally within a beam-and-screen room; two people interact on its surface. The device portrait removes architecture, while the sofa banner uses a stage-like backdrop.
brandMeaning: Lighting, environment and graphic intensity visibly vary by category.
application: Unify spatial and lighting principles without erasing category-specific product colours.
authorityAndLimits: This is the draft author's diagnosis, not a complete current-channel audit.

visibleEvidence: White serif statements occupy a black page beside a white-bordered image of a seated person using a dark foot device.
spatialReading: A cream outfit and white sofa contrast with blue walls. An arch, stairs, rear window and several lamps establish a domestic setting; the device rests on the rug beneath the person's feet.
brandMeaning: The proposition connects everyday stillness with a broader restoration narrative.
application: Borrow credible seated contact and domestic context for recovery-category imagery; simplify competing lamps and décor.
authorityAndLimits: Neither the pose nor the written arc demonstrates stress relief or renewed energy.

visibleEvidence: An eight-part contents list sits beside a red messaging panel and a forest sale banner with white display lettering and a red lower strip.
spatialReading: No interior is shown. A person in flowing yellow clothing reclines on a reddish chair among rocks, water and exposed roots; a dog occupies the foreground.
brandMeaning: The examples span core messaging and expressive promotional activation.
application: Borrow clear campaign hierarchy, not the elaborate outdoor staging as an everyday-room template.
authorityAndLimits: The embedded offer is campaign-specific. Scene authenticity, terrain support and practical motion clearance are unverified.

visibleEvidence: A black section divider frames an exposed blue mattress with visible Duroflex and airboost markings.
spatialReading: A frontal view centres the grey bed within a dark beam grid, translucent screens and an open garden edge. One person sits in a grey top and red shorts; another lies prone in pale clothing, supported on the mattress.
brandMeaning: Product visibility and informal interaction connect the proposition to ordinary companionship.
application: Borrow mattress legibility and supported contact; adapt the strongly themed architecture rather than copying it.
authorityAndLimits: The reference does not verify SKU construction; red clothing also conflicts with later draft restrictions.

visibleEvidence: A red lowercase serif Duroflex rendering, tiny tagline and large serif section title accompany rounded image tiles showing blue and mustard sofas, a mattress, recliner and surface detail.
spatialReading: Neutral walls, daylight and greenery recur, while a seaside arch introduces a more theatrical setting. Products remain dominant within individual tiles.
brandMeaning: The montage proposes category breadth within a shared warm environment.
application: Borrow the consistent neutral support around differing product colours; simplify destination-like scenery.
authorityAndLimits: The rendered wordmark and inset product labels are not validated identity or SKU masters.

visibleEvidence: The black/red headline states a shift from mattress to restoration. Five panels combine a bedroom, product-world boards and human-use examples.
spatialReading: The largest room has a low dark platform bed, cream bedding, olive throw and tall left opening with sheer curtains. Side light reveals wall texture and keeps a clear foreground.
brandMeaning: The proposition broadens Duroflex from a product category toward lived experience.
application: Borrow openness and quiet layering, but expose the exact mattress when product explanation is the objective.
authorityAndLimits: The dressed bed illustrates atmosphere, not identifiable mattress performance.

visibleEvidence: People stretch, recline, read and lie with eyes closed above three room references. The title highlights 'Energy' in red.
spatialReading: Pillows support heads and upper bodies. Below, a sunlit cream lounge, lamp-lit bedside corner and pale bedroom with red runner and ottoman show different rest settings.
brandMeaning: The stated stress-to-energy arc is illustrated mainly through stillness and relaxed activity.
application: Borrow supported poses and restrained domestic activity; avoid staging a dramatic before/after transformation.
authorityAndLimits: The collage does not establish emotional states, a chronological recovery sequence or health outcomes.

visibleEvidence: A large black/red serif title faces five small red subheads with black bullet points on an ivory field.
spatialReading: No room or person is shown; the right-hand list occupies only a narrow portion of the page.
brandMeaning: The text proposes visible cues for stress relief, restoration, trust, energy and innovation.
application: Translate these into observable shot choices rather than benefit claims.
authorityAndLimits: The page supplies propositions, not depicted product-quality or scientific evidence.

visibleEvidence: The red word 'quieter' anchors a serif headline beside repeated product, people and room boards plus a larger bedside crop.
spatialReading: The crop layers a bed edge, timber-looking cabinet, warm lamp, branch-filled vessel and foreground water carafe. Tight framing communicates proximity rather than architectural openness.
brandMeaning: Quietness is expressed through low-contrast surfaces and modest domestic actions.
application: Borrow tactile intimacy for supporting details; reduce accessories when the product must lead.
authorityAndLimits: This is a visual metaphor, not evidence of acoustic quietness or restoration efficacy.

visibleEvidence: The philosophy statement accompanies product boards, a cream lounge and a large wall vignette combining vertical slats, an arched niche and rough stone-looking texture.
spatialReading: A floating cabinet and recessed shelves organise ceramics, books and plants. Side light reveals depth; the lounge adds a low round table and woven-looking rug.
brandMeaning: Warmth is constructed through tonal relationships and tactile variation.
application: Borrow the restrained colour relationships; adapt by selecting fewer surfaces and ornaments.
authorityAndLimits: The text names a contemporary Indian direction; pixels do not establish geographic origin or material composition.

visibleEvidence: A sparse ivory page uses a black/red serif title and three vertically stacked style lists. GREEN, AMBER and RED headings are all rendered in red.
spatialReading: No room is shown; the categories are textual filters, not visual swatches.
brandMeaning: The proposition favours selective borrowing over stylistic imitation.
application: Evaluate reference features individually instead of importing an entire named style.
authorityAndLimits: These are draft preferences, not adopted exclusions or evidence that a particular room belongs to a style.

visibleEvidence: Five red principle headings with small black explanations sit opposite the large 'Approval before assets' title.
spatialReading: No room, product or person is depicted.
brandMeaning: The proposed filter balances calm with warmth, premium presentation with restraint, and human presence with unforced behaviour.
application: Use the principles as review questions before selecting surfaces, poses and layouts.
authorityAndLimits: The word 'Approval' describes a proposed process; this page grants no asset or quality approval.

visibleEvidence: Two bedrooms and two resting-person crops illustrate the proposed logo-independent signature. One room uses red art, cushions, a foreground throw and mattress trim; the other uses olive accents.
spatialReading: Both rooms employ pale walls and large openings. The people rest against pillows, with clothing and bedding visibly draped around supported bodies.
brandMeaning: The draft seeks recognition through environment and body language beyond a logo.
application: Borrow light and soft geometry; resolve excess red styling and preserve only verified SKU trim.
authorityAndLimits: No recognition test or authentic product specification is supplied.

visibleEvidence: A calm product montage is labelled DO; a crowded red bedroom with three smiling, outward-gesturing people is labelled DON'T.
spatialReading: Red walls, bedding, rugs and outfits compete with framed art, lamps and glossy-looking tables. Dense foreground props compress circulation; a bright glare intensifies the display-like scene.
brandMeaning: The contrast rejects simultaneous chromatic, decorative and performative intensity.
application: Borrow the clear comparison method; assess product hierarchy, usable space and supported natural activity separately.
authorityAndLimits: The negative example is exaggerated and does not establish a precise acceptance threshold.

visibleEvidence: A section divider gives most of its image area to a cream-and-olive bedroom.
spatialReading: The three-quarter view shows a low dark platform, upholstered-looking headboard, woven-looking rug and tall left garden opening. Sheers filter daylight; leaf shadows cross the textured wall. The right crop limits assessment of circulation.
brandMeaning: Architecture and light carry the calm more than decorative branding.
application: Borrow genuine wall space and indoor-outdoor depth; widen the frame when full SKU edges and access routes matter.
authorityAndLimits: No person, material specification or verified room scale is provided.

visibleEvidence: Bedroom, wall, lounge and product-board references support the statement 'Warm Indian modernism.'
spatialReading: Large openings, sheers, low furniture and pale textured surfaces recur. The lounge has an open route behind the sofa, while the wall vignette uses a recessed arch and floating cabinet.
brandMeaning: The proposition combines contemporary domestic warmth with an indoor-outdoor relationship.
application: Borrow openings and layered neutrals; adapt generous proportions and highly ordered styling to a believable home.
authorityAndLimits: Climate awareness and cultural specificity are stated aims, not verified properties of these references.

visibleEvidence: Two bedroom boards sit above a frontal green-bed image with an exposed grey-sided mattress.
spatialReading: The bed is centred against a tall pale wall, flanked by narrow sea-view openings and compact round bedside units. A timber-looking ceiling and bordered rug frame it; diagonal daylight crosses the wall.
brandMeaning: Symmetry and visible mattress edges prioritise product clarity.
application: Borrow the frontal product read; adapt side clearances, decorative rug and destination-like outlook.
authorityAndLimits: The pictured high green headboard does not directly illustrate every stated cue, including pale wood and low forms.

visibleEvidence: Living-world boards accompany a teal sofa on a taupe backdrop, a mustard footrest close-up with exposed mechanism and a pale upholstery detail against wine.
spatialReading: The lower images are product studies, not rooms. Upper insets show low seating, broad tables and warm interior-to-exterior views.
brandMeaning: Silhouette, surface and visible construction extend the architectural story into product detail.
application: Borrow complementary environment and close-detail coverage; preserve exact seams, upholstery and mechanism geometry.
authorityAndLimits: Social ease is stated but not enacted here; materials and mechanical operation remain unverified.

visibleEvidence: Five references accompany four named archetypes: bedroom, lounge, seaside-arch recliner, wall niche and lamp-lit bedside corner.
spatialReading: The bedroom and lounge receive strong side daylight. The recliner sits beneath a flower-framed arch; the bedside crop feels enclosed and intimate.
brandMeaning: The menu proposes different settings for reset, release, recovery and retail.
application: Borrow category-appropriate openness or intimacy; simplify theatrical scenery and clarify which image demonstrates each archetype.
authorityAndLimits: No identifiable retail zone is shown. The recliner image's darkened lower edge is not permission to add photographic fades.

visibleEvidence: A quiet-wall proposition is illustrated through a slatted niche wall, bedside corner, mattress board, restrained red-accent bedroom and crowded red display.
spatialReading: Broad pale wall areas support the beds, while the niche combines several textures and shelf objects. The crowded display interrupts surfaces with art, lamps and props.
brandMeaning: The intended distinction is background support versus visual competition.
application: Borrow low-contrast wall depth; simplify the multi-surface vignette rather than reproducing every layer.
authorityAndLimits: The mixed collage requires interpretation; not every included image is explicitly labelled positive or negative.

visibleEvidence: The heading says 'Approved surfaces' beside a niche wall, sunlit bedroom, room boards and warm bedside crop.
spatialReading: Slat rhythm, mottled wall appearance, rough stone-looking relief and soft curtains supply different scales of texture. Side light makes these visible without strong colour contrast.
brandMeaning: The draft favours tactile interest over graphic wall pattern.
application: Borrow one dominant wall treatment with quieter supporting surfaces; adapt texture density to the exact product.
authorityAndLimits: 'Approved' remains draft language. The listed limewash, travertine and other materials cannot be confirmed from these images.

visibleEvidence: The red display room appears twice beside contact sheets of identity, product and promotional assets.
spatialReading: Dense furniture, décor and saturated surfaces dominate the room; presenter-like gestures add activity. The contact sheets are graphic archives, not additional architectural examples.
brandMeaning: The stated rejection targets visual overload and showroom-like competition.
application: Avoid cumulative clutter; do not treat every historical asset visible in the contact sheets as rejected.
authorityAndLimits: Several listed exclusions, such as neon panels, are not clearly demonstrated. Small thumbnails do not support detailed asset judgements.

visibleEvidence: Bedroom, lounge and bedside references repeatedly show large woven-looking rugs, pale flooring and warm brown furniture; a brighter bedroom shows wood-looking floorboards.
spatialReading: Rugs define furniture zones and soften the foreground. Side lighting reveals pile or weave while shadows beneath beds and tables establish contact.
brandMeaning: Grounding comes from layered surfaces rather than reflective spectacle.
application: Borrow quiet floor continuity and coherent base shadows; keep rug edges and access routes plausible.
authorityAndLimits: The named wood species and floor finishes are proposals, not visually verified specifications.

visibleEvidence: The 'Skin-trust palette' page combines rumpled cream bedding, a textured chair, water carafe, mustard footrest detail and two bed scenes.
spatialReading: The bedside crop is tightly layered around a low round table and warm lamp. Wider bed references use neutral walls with green or red accents.
brandMeaning: Texture and approachable domestic objects suggest sensory warmth.
application: Borrow readable weave, drape and cushion modelling without modifying the SKU's actual surface.
authorityAndLimits: No skin contact is shown here; the images establish neither skin safety, fabric composition nor comfort performance.

visibleEvidence: People wear loose cream, sage and muted-rose clothing while sitting, reading, holding a mug or leaning together. A second panel shows textured bedding and a lamp-lit corner.
spatialReading: Bent legs, cushions and floor seating create close body-to-surface relationships. Hanging garments repeat the muted palette; foreground furniture makes the room crop intimate.
brandMeaning: Unforced activity links tactile surroundings to everyday living.
application: Borrow relaxed styling and small actions; verify weight-bearing contact and keep wardrobe secondary to the product.
authorityAndLimits: The listed fibres and 'breathability' are not demonstrated material properties.

visibleEvidence: A slatted niche wall, low round lounge table, bedside cabinet and product-world boards illustrate 'Warm craft.'
spatialReading: Grain-like markings and uneven pale surfaces contrast with soft upholstery. Left-side daylight grazes relief, while the lamp-lit crop adds amber warmth and closer object layering.
brandMeaning: Hard surfaces are positioned as tactile partners to softness, not cold technical scenery.
application: Borrow restrained surface contrast; reduce heavy stone-looking masses and shelf décor if they overpower the SKU.
authorityAndLimits: Stone type, wood species, terracotta and brushed-metal composition are not established by these references.

visibleEvidence: The nature page repeats a garden-opening bedroom, planted niche, cream lounge and category boards.
spatialReading: The bedroom connects interior and exterior through tall glazing, sheers and leaf shadows. Other examples rely more on potted plants, including trailing greenery in a recess and plants beside seating.
brandMeaning: Nature is proposed as part of spatial experience rather than a decorative badge.
application: Borrow framed views and source-consistent shadows; adapt plant placement into one coherent architectural zone.
authorityAndLimits: Courtyards and structural planters are stated options, but the visible evidence chiefly shows openings and pots.

visibleEvidence: The instruction 'Fewer, better plants' accompanies rooms containing both substantial greenery and several smaller potted accents.
spatialReading: The lounge has a large plant near the window, trailing niche greenery and tabletop planting. The bedside corner layers a tall branch-filled vessel with smaller plants around furniture.
brandMeaning: The intended hierarchy is one strong natural presence, though the examples are less selective.
application: Consolidate greenery and remove redundant small pots; retain clear circulation and the product silhouette.
authorityAndLimits: The imagery does not consistently demonstrate the stated reduction in scattered decoration.

visibleEvidence: Sunlit bedroom and lounge references accompany the proposal to own soft restorative light; product boards and a brighter red-trim bedroom complete the page.
spatialReading: Visible left openings motivate illumination. Leaf patterns, diagonal floor shadows and warm highlights reveal surfaces, although some sun edges are comparatively defined.
brandMeaning: Recognisability is proposed through a lighting character rather than room colour alone.
application: Borrow motivated daylight and gentle modelling; maintain exact product colour and coherent shadows without haze or blur treatments.
authorityAndLimits: Time of day and restorative effects cannot be established from the pictures.

visibleEvidence: A bedroom board with exposed blue-sided mattresses sits above two dressed beds: one cream/olive, one pale with red accents.
spatialReading: Tall openings, light bedding and readable bed edges support a fresh atmosphere. The olive room shows warm leaf shadows; the red-accent room is more evenly bright.
brandMeaning: The text proposes a morning mood for sleep products.
application: Borrow daylight clarity and open framing; adapt surrounding colours to the actual mattress rather than recolouring it blue-white.
authorityAndLimits: 'Morning' and 'breathable' describe intended presentation, not verified timing or airflow.

visibleEvidence: A large frontal green-bed scene is combined with bedroom boards, a warm bedside corner, pale upholstery against wine and a red-accent bedroom.
spatialReading: The green bed has clear mattress edges, compact side tables and narrow sea-view openings. Direct daylight crosses its pale wall; the other panels introduce warmer or more saturated lighting contexts.
brandMeaning: The proposition prioritises calm product legibility for explanatory channels.
application: Borrow clear silhouette and neutral exposure; standardise colour handling for catalogue use.
authorityAndLimits: The collage is not a consistent neutral-light specification or a current website sample.

visibleEvidence: An evening-mood statement accompanies a teal sofa on taupe, mustard mechanism detail, seaside-arch recliner, sunlit lounge and living-world board.
spatialReading: Soft studio modelling isolates the sofa, while the architectural references include bright exterior sky and substantial daylight rather than uniformly low evening light.
brandMeaning: Tactile richness is more consistently demonstrated than the stated wine/olive/walnut evening palette.
application: Borrow warm environmental support and detail coverage; preserve teal, mustard or other exact SKU colours.
authorityAndLimits: The examples do not establish a single approved evening treatment.

visibleEvidence: Neutral bedrooms with red art, cushions, runners, trim and an ottoman are contrasted with the crowded red display and category boards.
spatialReading: Pale walls and daylight keep the quieter rooms legible, but repeated red objects create several competing accents. The crowded room distributes red across almost every layer.
brandMeaning: The proposition separates brand recognition from an entirely red environment.
application: Borrow restrained graphic identification; resolve which environmental accents are permitted and preserve only verified product details.
authorityAndLimits: These examples conflict with the later draft prohibition on red bedding and props.

visibleEvidence: A written palette accompanies cream/olive rooms, blue and mustard sofas, muted clothing and product-world boards. Red remains prominent in the page's wordmark and headline.
spatialReading: Pale architectural fields provide continuity; darker upholstery and olive textiles create depth. Daylit openings and warm brown furniture connect the bedroom and lounge.
brandMeaning: The proposed world is neutral-led but not colourless.
application: Let the exact SKU anchor colour relationships; choose complementary room and wardrobe layers rather than forcing every listed hue.
authorityAndLimits: This is a descriptive draft palette, not measured swatches or an exhaustive product-colour rule.

visibleEvidence: The category-accent statement is illustrated by a large teal sofa, mustard footrest detail, beige recliner beneath an arch and a warm bedside corner.
spatialReading: The imagery alternates between isolated product study, theatrical exterior outlook and close domestic detail. No complete recovery-device setting is visible.
brandMeaning: The text proposes category variation without a change of identity.
application: Borrow neutral support and tactile continuity; adapt light and room context rather than enforcing category colours on products.
authorityAndLimits: Blue-white sleep and spa-tech recovery are not clearly demonstrated by this selection.

visibleEvidence: Two dense product-world boards and a portrait bedroom reference accompany a proposed 25–40% breathing-space target.
spatialReading: The bedroom contains genuine pale wall and floor area, but the bed fills much of its width and a red ottoman competes near the foreground. Large slide margins are outside the photograph.
brandMeaning: The intended hierarchy is one important product within a calm setting.
application: Create space through camera position and architecture—not white patches, masks or fades.
authorityAndLimits: The percentage is a draft proposal; these examples do not demonstrate a measured photographic ratio.

visibleEvidence: A red Duroflex wordmark and black/red serif headline accompany warm bedrooms, a bedside vignette and small reference boards. One bedroom contains red bedding accents and a red bench.
spatialReading: The largest bedroom uses a left terrace opening, sheer curtain, broad wall and low bed; lateral daylight leaves readable foreground floor.
brandMeaning: The stated breathing-space proposition is supported most clearly by architectural emptiness.
application: Borrow wall space and circulation; reduce decorative red rather than adding photographic fades or white patches.
authorityAndLimits: Slide margins are graphic space, not evidence of room geometry.

visibleEvidence: A bedside scene combines rumpled textiles, a glowing lamp, carafe and plants. Separate images show mustard upholstery above a mechanism and a green bed.
spatialReading: The close room crop layers foreground table, bed and chair; the frontal bed sits beneath a coffered ceiling between side openings.
brandMeaning: Texture supports the stated sensory proposition without establishing quality or performance.
application: Borrow varied surface scale and directional modelling; preserve the exact SKU’s fabric and construction.
authorityAndLimits: Visible grain cannot identify fibre, stone type or material composition.

visibleEvidence: The collage shows a carafe-and-book vignette, terrace bedroom, cream sectional, red-accented bed and a small human-activity board.
spatialReading: Low tables and rugs anchor furniture; daylight enters from side openings. Plants occupy edges and niches, while the principal seating and sleeping surfaces remain readable.
brandMeaning: Everyday objects suggest use rather than purely ornamental display.
application: Borrow reachable drinks, reading material and sparse bedside storage; adapt their positions to actual circulation and product access.
authorityAndLimits: The red artwork and cushion are illustrative choices, not an approved accessory prescription.

visibleEvidence: A carafe, tray, books and lamp accompany an arched shelf niche, slatted panel, floating cabinet, sectional, red-accented bedroom and clothing/people collage.
spatialReading: Side light articulates smooth, ribbed and rough-looking wall surfaces; the recessed shelves keep objects out of the foreground passage.
brandMeaning: The stated useful-object vocabulary is partly demonstrated through drinking, lighting and reading cues.
application: Borrow recessed storage and task-led props for bedroom or living moods; simplify redundant vessels and plants.
authorityAndLimits: The text names materials; the pictures establish appearance, not composition.

visibleEvidence: A crowded red room appears twice, with patterned furnishings, reflective ornaments, broad smiles and outstretched arms. Two inset contact sheets show assorted graphics and campaigns.
spatialReading: Foreground tables obstruct the bed’s approach; intense highlights and repeated red surfaces compete with the product.
brandMeaning: The rejection example illustrates accumulated visual noise, not simply the presence of accessories.
application: Use it as a negative diagnostic for clutter, competing highlights and theatrical presentation.
authorityAndLimits: Its placement does not establish that every small inset campaign has the same defects.

visibleEvidence: An arched niche, vertical slats, rough-looking wall, cream sectional, bedside vignette and green bed illustrate the stated Indian-modernity proposition.
spatialReading: The living room combines left-side curtains, a recessed shelf and a right passage leading toward another arch; layered beige and green maintain depth.
brandMeaning: Architectural integration carries the proposition more convincingly than decorative motifs.
application: Borrow shaded openings, tactile relief and connected rooms; adapt scale and detailing to the exact product.
authorityAndLimits: Indian origin, local craft and the listed materials cannot be authenticated from these images.

visibleEvidence: The page pairs a domestic niche with marketing contact sheets, bedroom boards, a red-accented bed and sofa references.
spatialReading: The principal image shows a floating cabinet, shelving and clear floor, not a store layout. Product displays appear only in separate reference images.
brandMeaning: “Store as home” is a stated retail ambition rather than a depicted implementation.
application: Borrow residential-scale display zones and restrained storage; add practical test areas, wayfinding and unobstructed routes.
authorityAndLimits: No actual retail circulation, capacity, accessibility or operating arrangement is demonstrated.

visibleEvidence: A world board, terrace bedroom, niche, sofa board and human-activity board accompany the pre-shoot checklist.
spatialReading: The bedroom connects a low bed to a planted exterior through a tall left opening; the niche supplies vertical rhythm and contained storage.
brandMeaning: The draft treats architecture, light, props and people as coordinated decisions.
application: Translate the checklist into a set plan around the exact SKU, including light direction, contact shadows, pathways and prop locations.
authorityAndLimits: The collage supplies mood relationships, not measured plans or a completed production lock.

visibleEvidence: A black divider uses a small red section label and large white serif title. A bordered image shows wine-coloured piped sleepwear on an olive recliner.
spatialReading: No room is shown. The tight studio crop includes bent knees, bare feet, a lowered gaze, a hand across the armrest and visible side controls.
brandMeaning: The pose illustrates inward attention rather than product presentation.
application: Borrow supported asymmetry and meaningful hand contact; check seat compression and cropped limbs.
authorityAndLimits: Clothing sheen is visible; fibre type and emotional release are not established.

visibleEvidence: A red section number and large black title introduce an enlarged board showing stretching, reading, shoulder-to-head contact and reclining.
spatialReading: Beds and seats support the figures within softly lit domestic fragments; cream clothing contrasts with deep-blue seating and a green headboard.
brandMeaning: The stated behaviour sequence becomes a vocabulary of recognisable resting actions.
application: Borrow product-supported gestures and off-camera attention; retain clear hands, feet and points of contact.
authorityAndLimits: The embedded board is cropped, and its red books, mugs and wine clothing complicate stricter red guidance.

visibleEvidence: Repeated boards show overhead stretching, reading, reclining, side-lying and seated cup-holding. Loose cream, sage, blue and muted pink clothing dominates.
spatialReading: Close framing prioritises bodies against pillows, headboards and seating; windows, plants and storage provide peripheral domestic context.
brandMeaning: “Quietly aspirational Indians” is the page’s stated audience proposition, not a demographic finding from the portraits.
application: Borrow ordinary activities and relaxed styling across bedroom and seating categories.
authorityAndLimits: Nationality, personal values, relationships and genuine wellbeing cannot be inferred from appearance.

visibleEvidence: The collage includes different hair textures, a grey-bearded figure, small smiles, closed eyes, reading poses and a polished red-accented bedroom.
spatialReading: Softly lit close views emphasise faces and resting postures; the separate bedroom uses a large side window and restrained neutral surfaces.
brandMeaning: Accessible casting is proposed, but the highly curated montage does not itself demonstrate unretouched authenticity.
application: Direct attention toward an activity and believable body support rather than an idealised camera pose.
authorityAndLimits: Casting accessibility and “natural beauty” are subjective propositions, not verifiable image attributes.

visibleEvidence: Resting-person boards sit beside an empty cream recliner framed by an arch and vivid flowering foliage, plus a cream sectional room.
spatialReading: The recliner’s raised footrest faces the camera against a scenic opening and dark foreground; the living room instead uses domestic side light and a low table.
brandMeaning: The text proposes life-stage breadth, while the pictures primarily demonstrate varied resting poses.
application: Borrow category-relevant activities; adapt the scenic chair setting into a grounded home.
authorityAndLimits: The stated parent and family coverage is not demonstrated by identifiable family interactions.

visibleEvidence: Stretching, hands-behind-head reclining, reading and side-lying recur alongside sofa references and an unoccupied recliner.

brandMeaning: The contracted-to-ready body arc is stated, but no continuous before-and-after sequence is depicted.
application: Storyboard small, supported changes around one exact product, maintaining consistent body contact and room geometry.
authorityAndLimits: These stills cannot establish stress reduction, recovery or a causal bodily transformation.

visibleEvidence: The page shows joined hands overhead, open elbows, reading, closed eyes, leaning together and floor-seated poses; an empty recliner also appears.
spatialReading: Tight domestic crops foreground pillow, backrest and armrest contact, with muted clothing separating figures from pale bedding or blue seating.
brandMeaning: The gesture list favours activity-based rest over explicit selling.
application: Borrow believable hand–book interaction and supported head, hip and foot positions; adapt gestures to each product.
authorityAndLimits: “Approved gestures” is a draft heading, not evidence of final approval or anatomical validation.

visibleEvidence: Broad camera-facing smiles and expansive standing gestures dominate the repeated red-room example; smaller contact sheets surround it.
spatialReading: People, reflective décor, floral art and red textiles compete with the central bed. Bright frontal highlights intensify the staged presentation.
brandMeaning: The stated rejection concerns advertising performance rather than everyday product use.
application: Replace presenter-style gestures with a specific resting activity and credible contact with the furniture.
authorityAndLimits: Not every listed rejection, such as thumbs-up or pointing, is clearly demonstrated in the principal image.

visibleEvidence: Closed eyes, small smiles, reading and shoulder-to-head contact appear beside a warmly lit bedside vignette with a carafe and lamp.
spatialReading: Body crops remain intimate; the empty vignette builds atmosphere through layered textiles, foreground objects and a warm pool of lamplight.
brandMeaning: The pictures support restrained expression, while relief and post-rest energy remain stated interpretations.
application: Direct soft attention, unforced expressions and purposeful hands rather than exaggerated happiness.
authorityAndLimits: Internal emotions and a product’s effect on them cannot be verified from posed or illustrative stills.

visibleEvidence: Two figures share seating with one head resting against the other; surrounding boards show individual reading, cup-holding and resting. A cream sectional room is unoccupied.
spatialReading: Shared seating brings bodies close, while the room reference preserves a central table zone and a passage at the right.
brandMeaning: Companionship is suggested through proximity and contact rather than matching camera poses.
application: Borrow small shared rituals with plausible shoulder support, seat compression and independent limb positions.
authorityAndLimits: Actual relationships and the broader family proposition are not established by these images.

visibleEvidence: Static stretching and reclining portraits accompany sofa references and a cream chair with its footrest extended beneath a scenic arch.
spatialReading: The room fragments offer backrest and pillow support; the standalone chair shows clearance in front but no person moving through it.
brandMeaning: Slow transitions are a proposed movement quality, not a visible temporal result.
application: Plan settling, turning and rising as separate supported actions with consistent light and clear foot placement.
authorityAndLimits: No reviewed video establishes movement speed, mechanism operation or continuity between poses.

visibleEvidence: Loose pale shirts, sage tops, muted mauve sets, soft-looking trousers and hanging garments appear with blue and pink sleepwear.
spatialReading: Seated knees and bent elbows create visible folds; pale garments merge gently with bedding, while darker clothing separates against lighter seating.
brandMeaning: The stated tactile wardrobe direction is conveyed through drape and everyday silhouettes.
application: Borrow low-pattern, relaxed styling while maintaining enough tonal separation to read body–product contact.

brandMeaning: Earthy product colour supports warmth, while the ocean panorama sustains a luxury-retreat mood.
application: Retain the rust SKU and structural legibility; simplify the floor/rug relationship and surrounding spectacle.
authorityAndLimits: Rust upholstery is product colour, not evidence of a brand-red rule.

visibleEvidence: A person in a white athletic-style top rests on a textured white pillow. A black footer reads “100% Latex. Cool by Nature.” in white italics beside orange chevrons; thin grid lines have orange square markers.

application: Borrow clear contact visibility, not the lighting or graphics as universal rules.
authorityAndLimits: Composition and cooling are stated claims, not visually demonstrated facts.
